This is not a dodge, and row 1 earned its place. Without it, `R` = 1.61 with `p_upper` = 0.99 would

accepted set reaches strictly **deeper** into the ranking than `finding:0013`'s **global top-50**

prior informs power only — the confirmatory test **measures the accepted set's own precision directly**
(full census), so nothing rides on borrowing the 0.44.

title: Blind census of the n=10000 near-miss set: 5/36 form-equivalent (p_hat=0.139,
paragraph:
The blind census that `finding:0016` and `interpretation:0208` explicitly deferred is now
**run** (`pre-registration:0023`; Keith adjudicated 2026-07-08). A full blind census of the
`N_accepted = 36` near-miss accepted set `A` (no subsample; `n_adj = 36`) — each accepted pair
shown as two neutrally-labeled skeletons with curated↔corpus orientation randomized, rows
shuffled, seed derived from the frozen manifest descriptor hash, and **no score / rank / pair
id / curated-vs-corpus tag** exposed — returned **`k = 5` form-equivalent**, **p̂ = 0.139**,
Wilson-95 **[0.061, 0.287]**. This is **below both** pre-registered certification thresholds
(`p̂ ≥ 0.30` and `p_lower95 ≥ 0.20`), so `threshold-freeze.json` certifies **`status =
uncalibrated`**: the near-miss arm **fails certification** as a coverage estimator and is **not
calibration-ready** in this frozen cycle. This **amends `finding:0016`** by converting its
uncalibrated "recovers all 36" into a measured precision, and **confirms `finding:0016`'s own
proposition** that the near-miss 36/36 is "a candidate set a census would prune, not a coverage
estimate" — the census pruned it to 5.

title: Fixed-margin incidence null for the catalog''s topology claims: is the reported
paragraph:
**A4.1 — WITHDRAWN: the "18.4% margin-forced self-loop floor."** Amendment 2 registered, as a
fail-closed abort condition, that the realized self-loop rate must not fall below 18.4%, described as
"forced by the margins." **That is wrong.** 18.4% is `p_tr(A_obs)` — the no-trade-row-pair rate of the
**observed** matrix. Whether a row's support is nested in another's depends on the **current
assignment**, not on the row and column sums, so the no-trade fraction **changes as the chain moves**.
A correct, uniform chain that wandered into a region with fewer nested rows would have realized a lower
self-loop rate and been **aborted by my own assertion**. Tradable pairs also contribute identity draws
with probability `1/C(u+l, u)`, so total self-loop probability is state-dependent for two independent
reasons.

title: Are cross-domain analogies an artifact of the analytic-tractability filter?
paragraph:
**Cross-domain analogies are not an artifact of a cross-domain-specific analytic-tractability
filter.** On the 152 curated cross-domain `relatedTo` edges, solvable–solvable endpoints are
enriched over a domain-stratified permutation null (`EF_cross` = +0.151) — but on the 385
within-domain edges the enrichment is approximately **twice as large on its own attainable-headroom
scale** (`EF_within` = +0.295). The primary statistic `ΔEF` = −0.144 against a critical value of
0.335 (p = 0.839, α = 0.01, B = 20,000), stable across all five pre-registered variants and not
hub-dependent. The 95% confidence set for `EF_cross` is [−0.45, 0.15]; **under the registered
exponential-tilt construction (0.05 grid)** the "substantial" band of ≥ 0.50 is excluded, in a design
with 0.845 power there.

paragraph: **The denominator is the ATTAINABLE headroom, not the nominal edge count.** Version 1 divided by `N_cross = 152`, which assumed all 152 cross edges *could* be solvable–solvable. **They cannot.** The domain marginals fix how many tractable labels each domain holds and the topology fixes which nodes are endpoints; the attainable maximum over the permutation support is **C_max = 99 of 152 (65%)** against a chance floor of 53.1 (34.9%). paragraph:
**Why the 100-shuffle null is dropped — and it is NOT because it is slow.** `compare_partitions`
carries its **own** permutation null (`graph-analysis.py:453`): it shuffles community **labels** while
holding the **graph fixed**, answering *"is this partition better aligned to chapters than chance?"*.
That is **a different, unregistered null**. The registered null resamples **the graph** at fixed margins.
Its outputs (`null_NMI_mean`, `sigmas_above_null`) are read by **no registered statistic**, and running
a nested null inside each draw of another null is a **category error**, not merely an expense. It would
still be dropped if it were free.

title: Fixed-margin incidence null for the catalog''s topology claims: is the reported
paragraph:
**`R` is NOT a fraction forced, explained, or accounted for.** Version 1 of this document called it a
"construction fraction" and glossed `R = 0.80` as "80% of the reported value is forced by the
margins." That is an overclaim, and for `beta_1` it is close to meaningless: `beta_1` is a nonlinear
functional of the complex with **no additive decomposition**, so a null mean of 8.8 against an
observed 11 does **not** license "8.8 cycles were forced and 2.2 were special." Cycles are not
additively partitionable into forced and free ones. The same objection applies with less force to
clustering and modularity, which are also non-additive in the incidence. `R` identifies a
**magnitude comparison** and never a variance or causal decomposition. The names and glosses are
corrected throughout; the 0.50 and 0.80 thresholds are retained as registered **relative-magnitude**
thresholds, which is what they always operationally were.

title: Analytic-tractability-filter confound test: does shared solvability manufacture
paragraph: The design's honest limit: **it is powered to adjudicate "substantial vs. not" (0.845 power at 0.50), and it is not powered to characterize a partial filter** (31% power at 0.30). The 80% crossing sits just below the threshold, in (0.45, 0.50].
